dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm quite curious as to how this will end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sort of end are we talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: I mean the end of a play, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: Or... Well, there are some cases that have gone into session several times, but with no result. To be honest, they seem all the same to me.

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: Hmm. Let's review the plot again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound like a very rigorous distinction to me.

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: But does it matter, really? A criminal is a criminal — someone who's done wrong. Any case involving them is sure to become a talking point regardless.

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: And I'm a law-abiding citizen — I'm never going to touch the law's bottom line.

dialogues.speaker: Corneille
dialogues.text: Besides, watching trials is a way of studying the law as well.
